title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
snippet: Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. Existing methods typically learn these tasks jointly, a demanding objective given the scarcity of 4D supervision. We show that strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models provide an effective foundation: lifted trajectories, with occluded segments simply interpolated, already rival dedicated 3D trackers using the same geometry. However, lifted trajectories inherit correspondence and depth errors, and under occlusion, …
summary: ReLift is a paper on dense 3D tracking from monocular video. It lifts trajectories from pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models, then repairs the errors, especially under occlusion, instead of learning everything jointly.
whyItMatters: It shows that composing strong pretrained models can rival dedicated 3D trackers despite scarce 4D supervision.

snippet: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot…
summary: MoviEdit is a framework for editing long, multi-shot videos coherently across scene, viewpoint and subject changes. It comes with automatic data-generation pipelines for cross-shot supervision plus modeling and evaluation components.

title: Nvidia RTX Spark encrypted firmware slows inference speed to 35% on Linux

title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
snippet: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiot…
summary: DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model to extract compact latent actions that transfer across embodiments and appearances.

title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
snippet: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful s…
summary: Axion 1.0 is a fully open agent foundation model trained in just three stages: two light SFT stages then reinforcement learning, skipping mid-training, DPO and on-policy distillation.
whyItMatters: A simpler open recipe for agentic models lowers the bar for teams training their own.

title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
snippet: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reason…
summary: LoCo is a local preference learning method that compresses reasoning by detecting overthinking states in a model's own traces and teaching it to stop once it has enough information.
whyItMatters: Shorter chains of thought cut inference cost for reasoning models.

title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
snippet: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of re…
summary: ToolSpace synthesizes agent training environments tool-first, mining dependencies from real MCP execution traces so tool interfaces and cross-environment tasks are grounded.
whyItMatters: Better synthetic MCP environments could improve training of long-horizon tool-using agents.

title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
snippet: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform. "One of the most consistent concerns we've heard is that it's not clearly disclosed when AI has been used to create a mod," according to the post from site owner Victor "Foledinho" Folmann. "We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognise that there's a lot more we can do to make tha…
summary: Nexus Mods will require authors to declare whether AI was used in new mod uploads, expanding its existing AI-generated and AI-assisted tags.
whyItMatters: It's a notable example of a major creative community mandating AI disclosure.
